title: Armed Ojama vs Super Quant: turns 1–3
description:
You're on **Armed Ojama**, going first against a friend's **Super Quant** deck. Turn 1 builds **Armed Dragon LV7** and **XYZ-Dragon Cannon**, turn 2 is Friend's answer, and turn 3 recycles your Ojamas and wins a fight.

Press **→** to step through.

p2.name: Friend
cards: Super Quantal Mech King Great Magnus

steps.label: Turn 1: you go first
steps.narration:
The player going first **doesn't draw** on turn 1, so you start with just your 5 cards.

The plan: turn this hand into **Armed Dragon LV7** and **XYZ-Dragon Cannon**, while keeping **Ash Blossom** in hand for Friend's turn.

*Note: the hand from the video line was Ojamatch, Ojamagic, Ojamassimilation, Fusion Tag and Ash. That doesn't work with one copy of each Ojama (see step 3), so this replay swaps Ojamagic and Fusion Tag for Ojama Green and Ojama Black.*

steps.label: Activate Ojamatch
steps.narration:
**Ojamatch** is a Quick-Play Spell. Its **cost** is sending an "Ojama" card from your hand to the GY, so **Ojama Green** goes.

Costs are paid when you activate, before anything can respond. That's why Ojama Green is already in the GY while Ojamatch is still waiting to resolve.

actions.label: Ojamatch: add an Ojama + an Armed Dragon

steps.label: Ojamatch resolves
steps.narration:
Ojamatch adds **1 Ojama monster with a different name** from the card you sent (so not Green) and **1 "Armed Dragon" monster**. You take **Ojama Yellow** and **Armed Dragon Thunder LV3**.

**Why not Ojamagic as the cost, like the video?** Ojamagic adds Green, Yellow *and* Black, but only if all three are still in your Deck ([it's all or nothing](https://yugipedia.com/wiki/Card_Rulings:Ojamagic)). Its effect would activate *after* Ojamatch resolves, and Ojamatch has to take one of the three, so with one copy of each Ojama, Ojamagic would add nothing.

steps.label: Normal Summon Thunder LV3
steps.narration:
Right after resolving, Ojamatch lets you **Normal Summon** one of the two cards. That uses up your one Normal Summon for the turn.

It has to be **Thunder LV3**: a Level 5 monster like Thunder LV5 would need a Tribute, and your field is empty.

steps.label: Thunder LV3: level up
steps.narration:
**Thunder LV3**'s effect: send 1 monster from your hand to the GY as a cost (**Ojama Yellow**), then Thunder LV3 sends *itself* to the GY and Special Summons a Level 5 or lower "Armed Dragon" from your hand or Deck.

Notice the Ojamas are piling up in the GY. That's on purpose: **Ojamassimilation** can use Ojamas from the GY later.

steps.label: Special Summon Thunder LV5
steps.narration:
Thunder LV3 goes to the GY and **Armed Dragon Thunder LV5** comes out of the Deck.

Thunder LV3 also has a "draw 1" effect, but only when it's sent to the GY **as a cost** for a Dragon's effect. Here it sent itself as part of the *resolution*, so it doesn't draw.

On the field (and in the GY), Thunder LV5's name **becomes "Armed Dragon LV5"**. That matters in the next step.

modifier.label: Its name becomes "Armed Dragon LV5" on the field

steps.label: Thunder LV5: level up
steps.narration: Same trick, one level higher. Send a monster from your hand as the cost (**Ojama Black**), then Thunder LV5 sends itself to the GY and Special Summons a Level 7 or lower "Armed Dragon" from your hand or Deck.

steps.label: Special Summon Armed Dragon LV7
steps.narration:
**Armed Dragon LV7** (2800 ATK) arrives. LV7 *"must be Special Summoned by 'Armed Dragon LV5'"*, and Thunder LV5 counts because its name was "Armed Dragon LV5" on the field.

This is the **first material for the boss**. Armed Dragon Catapult Cannon needs LV7 and VWXYZ to have both been properly Special Summoned at some point this duel.

steps.label: Activate Ojamassimilation
steps.narration:
**Ojamassimilation**: reveal a LIGHT Machine Fusion Monster from your Extra Deck (**XYZ-Dragon Cannon**) and banish any number of Ojama monsters from your hand, field or GY as the cost.

You banish all **3 Ojamas from the GY**. Every card you've discarded so far is paying off.

steps.label: Summon X, Y and Z
steps.narration: Three Ojamas banished means **three materials** Special Summoned, each with a different name listed on XYZ-Dragon Cannon: **X-Head Cannon**, **Y-Dragon Head** and **Z-Metal Tank**, straight from the Deck.

steps.label: XYZ-Dragon Cannon
steps.narration:
**XYZ-Dragon Cannon** (2800 ATK) is Special Summoned from the Extra Deck by **banishing X, Y and Z** from your field. No Polymerization needed.

This isn't a *Fusion Summon*, even though XYZ is a Fusion Monster. That distinction comes back when we talk about Fusion Tag at the end.

steps.label: End turn 1
steps.narration:
Your board: **Armed Dragon LV7** and **XYZ-Dragon Cannon**, both 2800 ATK. In hand: **Ash Blossom**.

Ash is a **hand trap**: you discard it during *Friend's* turn to negate an effect that searches the Deck, Special Summons from the Deck, or sends from the Deck to the GY. Holding it is the whole point.

steps.label: Turn 2: Friend draws
steps.narration: Friend's turn. They draw for the turn and go to their Main Phase.

steps.label: Normal Summon Blue Layer
steps.narration:
Friend Normal Summons **Super Quantum Blue Layer**, one of the Super Quant "pilots". When it's summoned, it **adds a Super Quant card from the Deck to the hand**.

That's a search from the Deck, exactly what **Ash Blossom** can stop.

steps.label: You chain Ash Blossom
steps.narration:
You respond: discard **Ash Blossom** (that's its cost) to negate the search. Ash becomes **Chain Link 2** on top of Blue Layer's effect.

Chains resolve **last in, first out**, so Ash will resolve before the search does.

steps.label: Friend chains Black Layer
steps.narration:
Friend has an answer. **Super Quantum Black Layer** can Special Summon itself from the hand *when the opponent activates a monster effect*. Ash Blossom is a monster effect, so your Ash lets Black Layer in.

Black Layer becomes **Chain Link 3**. This is the "makes a Zord anyway" part of the story.

steps.label: Chain Link 3: Black Layer
steps.narration: The chain starts resolving from the top. Black Layer's effect **discards 1 other card** (**Red Layer**) and Special Summons Black Layer from the hand.

steps.label: Chain Links 2 and 1
steps.narration:
**Chain Link 2** (Ash Blossom) resolves and negates the search. Then **Chain Link 1** (Blue Layer's search) resolves as a negated effect and does nothing.

Ash did its job, but it cost you your only hand trap *and* opened the door for Black Layer. Trade-offs like this are what make Yu-Gi-Oh interesting.

steps.label: Black Layer becomes Magnaliger
steps.narration:
Black Layer was Special Summoned, so its next effect triggers. It Xyz Summons a **"Super Quantal Mech Beast"** (the "Zord") from the Extra Deck **using itself as material**, then **attaches a Super Quant monster from the GY**.

Friend picks **Super Quantal Mech Beast Magnaliger** (2600 ATK) and attaches **Red Layer**. Xyz materials sit *under* the monster (the cards peeking out behind it).

steps.label: Magnaliger targets XYZ
steps.narration:
Magnaliger's effect: **detach 1 material** (the cost) and target 1 monster on the field to destroy. Friend detaches **Red Layer** and targets **XYZ-Dragon Cannon**.

With Red Layer attached, this was a Quick Effect usable on either player's turn. Detaching Red Layer turns that off, which matters next turn.

steps.label: XYZ-Dragon Cannon is destroyed
steps.narration:
**XYZ-Dragon Cannon is destroyed** and goes to your GY (a destroyed Fusion Monster goes to the GY, not back to the Extra Deck). X, Y and Z stay banished.

*The original story had the Zord bounce XYZ to the Extra Deck. No Super Quant Mech Beast does that, so this uses Magnaliger's real destroy effect.* Red Layer's own GY effect has nothing to revive, so it does nothing.

steps.label: Activate Magnacarrier
steps.narration: Friend activates the Field Spell **Super Quantal Mech Ship Magnacarrier**. Its cost is **discarding 1 card** (**Magnaslayer**). It targets a Super Quantum monster they control, here **Blue Layer**.

actions.label: Magnacarrier: Xyz Summon a Mech Beast

steps.label: Blue Layer becomes Grampulse
steps.narration:
Magnacarrier Xyz Summons a Mech Beast **with the same Attribute** as the target, using it as material. Blue Layer is WATER, so it becomes **Super Quantal Mech Beast Grampulse** (WATER, 1800 ATK).

With Blue Layer as material, Grampulse can destroy a Spell/Trap as a **Quick Effect**. Worth remembering before you set anything.

steps.label: No attack, end turn 2
steps.narration:
Friend doesn't attack. Magnaliger (2600) and Grampulse (1800) would both lose to **Armed Dragon LV7** (2800), and Magnaliger has already used its once-per-turn destroy.

You're down XYZ-Dragon Cannon and Ash Blossom, but LV7 is still standing.

steps.label: Turn 3: you draw
steps.narration: Your turn. You draw **Forbidden Droplet**.

steps.label: Ojamassimilation from the GY
steps.narration:
Ojamassimilation has a second effect **in the GY**: banish it (the cost), then target 3 of your banished Ojama monsters, shuffle them into the Deck, and draw 1.

Your three Ojamas were banished on turn 1, so they come back into the Deck.

steps.label: Shuffle the Ojamas in, draw 1
steps.narration:
Green, Yellow and Black go back into the Deck, which is shuffled, and you draw 1. A real draw is random. In this replay it's **Ojamagic**.

This is the key setup for the next step: **all three Ojamas are in the Deck again**.

steps.label: Forbidden Droplet
steps.narration:
**Ojamagic can't be activated from your hand.** It only does something when it's *sent* from the hand or field to the GY. (*The original story activated it. That isn't allowed.*)

So send it as a cost instead. **Forbidden Droplet**: send any number of other cards from your hand/field to the GY, and choose that many of Friend's Effect Monsters. You send **Ojamagic** and choose **Magnaliger**.

Because you sent a **Spell**, Friend can't respond with Spells. Grampulse could still destroy Droplet in response, but a Quick-Play Spell still resolves if it's destroyed on the chain, so it wouldn't help.

steps.label: Magnaliger is halved and negated
steps.narration: Until the end of this turn, Magnaliger's **ATK is halved** (2600 → **1300**) and its **effects are negated**. The card detail panel shows both (click Magnaliger).

steps.label: Ojamagic: add the Ojama trio
steps.narration:
**Ojamagic** was sent from your hand to the GY, so its effect activates: add **Ojama Green, Ojama Yellow and Ojama Black** from the Deck.

It works this time because all three are in the Deck, thanks to Ojamassimilation. Compare that with step 3 on turn 1.

actions.label: Ojamagic: add Green, Yellow and Black

steps.label: LV7 attacks Magnaliger
steps.narration: Battle Phase. **Armed Dragon LV7** (2800) attacks **Magnaliger** (now 1300).

steps.label: Magnaliger is destroyed
steps.narration: 2800 beats 1300: **Magnaliger is destroyed by battle** and Friend takes the difference, **1500 damage**. Its remaining material (Black Layer) goes to the GY with it, and Droplet's changes vanish because Magnaliger left the field.

steps.label: End turn 3: the road to the boss
steps.narration:
End of turn 3: **Armed Dragon LV7** on the field and **Green, Yellow and Black** in hand. Friend is on 6500 LP with Grampulse.

**The route to Armed Dragon Catapult Cannon** from here: **Ojamassimilation** revealing **VW-Tiger Catapult** banishes 2 Ojamas to summon **V-Tiger Jet** + **W-Wing Catapult**, then banish those for **VW-Tiger Catapult**. You'd also need a new **XYZ-Dragon Cannon** (yours is in the GY and can't be Special Summoned from there). Then banish VW + XYZ for **VWXYZ-Dragon Catapult Cannon**, and finally banish **VWXYZ + LV7** for the boss.

*Fusion Tag caveat: the video renames a spare monster with Fusion Tag to stand in for a missing piece. Fusion Tag's current text only applies "if used for a **Fusion Summon**", and these Machines are summoned by banishing, not Fusion Summoned. Check that ruling before counting on it.*
